reasoning: The lectures separate naturally into XR foundations, psycho-physiological issues, hardware/software/tracking, human factors, user-centered development, experience optimization, resource optimization, and practical Unity implementation. I kept optimization split because UX/navigation optimization and rendering-resource optimization require different knowledge. Lecture 63 was assigned to the foundational goal because it consolidates course scope and further learning.

G1.goal: Explain the foundational landscape of extended reality by positioning virtual, augmented, and mixed reality, describing application domains, system categories, historical evolution, and directions for further learning.
G1.achieves: Gives the learner the terminology, conceptual map, and motivational context needed to engage with XR hardware, human factors, development, and optimization.

G2.goal: Analyze the central issues and psycho-physiological constraints of XR systems, including immersion, presence, AR display and tracking challenges, and the causes, measurement, and mitigation of cybersickness.
G2.achieves: Enables the learner to recognize user-facing limitations and comfort risks when designing, implementing, or evaluating XR systems.

G3.goal: Identify and evaluate XR hardware, software, and tracking components, including VR and AR devices, input and output subsystems, tracking pipelines, and development platforms.
G3.achieves: Lets the learner select and reason about the technical platform for an XR system before building it.

G4.goal: Explain how human perception, sensory physiology, and interactive-system principles shape XR experience design and usability.
G4.achieves: Prepares the learner to evaluate and design visual, auditory, haptic, and interaction features that support presence while reducing discomfort.

G5.goal: Apply a user-centered, iterative XR development lifecycle to gather requirements, design interfaces and interactions, implement prototypes, and evaluate usability in the Majuli case study.
G5.achieves: Gives the learner a structured process for taking an XR system from problem definition to an evaluated implementation.

G6.goal: Optimize VR navigation and tour experience by modeling walking behavior, travel time, and cybersickness constraints to produce usable system-controlled paths.
G6.achieves: Enables the learner to reduce exposure duration and cybersickness while preserving presence and point-of-interest coverage in a virtual tour.

G7.goal: Analyze VR resource requirements by explaining computer-graphics rendering, the 3D viewing pipeline, GPU-based implementation, and platform-specific content optimization.
G7.achieves: Lets the learner identify where storage, computation, and network resources are consumed and choose optimization strategies for real-time XR delivery.

G8.goal: Build and preview a basic interactive XR or AR prototype in Unity by configuring the environment and using graphics, physics, animation, audio, C# scripting, and an AR SDK.
G8.achieves: Provides practical hands-on capability to connect XR concepts to a working application and demonstrate a simple AR or VR scene.
